name: remote-ios-teamless-signing
goal: Simulator products are signed ad hoc and name no Apple team or account anywhere, including the simulated entitlements Xcode links into the executable; the build verification rejects a product that does.

steps.title: Identify the regression, prior working behavior, root cause, and evidence.
steps.evidence: Regression against the standing rule that no Apple team or account is borrowed. Every simulator product built with CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO DEVELOPMENT_TEAM= carried application-identifier <team>.com.dafuga.harness in the simulated entitlements linked into the executable (App.app-Simulated.xcent), where <team> is a team of an account signed in to Xcode on this Mac. Root cause: Xcode injects base entitlements and prefixes the identifier with an account team even when no team is named; CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual, AppIdentifierPrefix= and TeamIdentifierPrefix= do not change it. The old verification read only the code signature (TeamIdentifier=not set) and accepted it. Seen first in the simulator Keychain database, whose item group had the team prefix.

steps.title: Write and run a failing regression test that faithfully reproduces the defect; record proof.
steps.evidence: packages/desktop/test/ios-simulator-entitlements.test.ts (generated with harness generate test; sha256 ce812e950703561b) builds real executables with the linker and codesign. Against the unrepaired verification: 4 failed, 1 passed (the control). Failures: a team-prefixed identifier, a declared team identifier and missing entitlements were all accepted, and the build did not name its own entitlements. The real Release product built the old way was also accepted as 'ad hoc, no team'. Log /tmp/harness-ios-teamless-red.log.

steps.title: Propose a root-cause repair and an automated guard for the identified failure.
steps.evidence: Repair: the build names its own entitlements file (ios/App/Simulator.entitlements, the app identifier alone) and sets CODE_SIGN_INJECT_BASE_ENTITLEMENTS=NO so Xcode adds none. Guard: verifiedSignature reads the product after every build and every re-signing: valid ad hoc signature, no team in the signature, simulated entitlements present and naming the app alone, no team-prefixed identifier, team identifier key or provisioning profile in any file of the product. It is part of the normal build command, so a build that names a team fails.

steps.title: Implement the repair and wire the prevention test or guard into normal project verification.
steps.evidence: scripts/ios-build-options.ts (simulatorSigning, simulatorEntitlements), scripts/ios-products.ts (accountProblem, verifiedSignature), scripts/build-ios-simulator.ts (fails on any verification error), ios/App/Simulator.entitlements. The guard runs inside bun run ios:build:simulator for every configuration and for the fixture copy.

steps.title: Repeat repair and the same unchanged regression test until it passes; record passing proof.
steps.evidence: Same unchanged file (sha256 ce812e950703561b): 5 passed, with test/ios-build-options.test.ts 8 passed. Log /tmp/harness-ios-teamless-green.log. Rebuilt products: Debug, its TEST ONLY fixture copy and Release all print 'signature ad hoc, no team, no account'.

steps.title: In an isolated fixture or temporary workspace, prove reintroducing the original failure makes the guard fail; restore and prove it passes.
steps.evidence: Isolated fixture /tmp/harness-team-prefix-fixture/App.app is the Release product built before the repair. The guard rejects it: 'A team of an account is named in App.' (exit 1, /tmp/harness-ios-teamless-guard.log). After the repair the rebuilt Release product at the normal path passes the same guard. --fixture --release is still refused before anything is built (exit 2).

steps.title: Repeat until the guard and relevant project checks pass; verify affected UI flows with fresh inspected screenshots and keep pending while proof fails.
